// Release Notes Template (Self-Managed)
// Use for a Self-Managed per-release changelog page — one page per release line
// (main = current line; v/26.1, v/25.3 = older supported lines).
// Other products are out of scope or pending: see the "Scope for this standard"
// table in resources/writing-style/release-notes.md.
// Reader question: "What changed in each release?"
// Follow the entry standard in resources/writing-style/release-notes.md — it defines
// the entry bar (present-tense outcome, body required, no PR/author/commit noise),
// the category set and order, the version-heading format, and the page structure.

= Redpanda Release Notes
:description: Detailed release notes for each Redpanda patch release, organized by version.
:page-topic-type: reference
// Floor version for the release-notes automation: only releases newer than this are added automatically.
:earliest-tracked-version: [X.Y.Z]

// Intro: 1-2 sentences. What the page covers, and where the curated highlights live.
This page lists the changes in each Redpanda release from version {earliest-tracked-version} onward, organized by version. For a curated summary of the major features in this release line, see xref:get-started:release-notes/redpanda.adoc[What's New].

// One section per release, newest first. Heading is the version and release date on one
// line: v<version> (<YYYY-MM-DD>). The date is authored — the release captain writes it
// (see the standard); there is no timezone label.
// Source line: the published release body's hash, directly under the heading.
// It does not render. See the standard and the sm-release-notes skill.
// - When you scaffold a page: skip this line with the example section. The
//   curated section carries its own source line.
// - When you write a section by hand: replace v[X.Y.Z] and the [hash ...]
//   placeholder. Compute the hash with the skill's command.
// - Delete the line in two cases: the release is unpublished (no release
//   yet, or a body that lists no changes), or the section comes from a
//   changelog that differs from the published body.
// Never merge the page with a placeholder still in place.
== v[X.Y.Z] ([YYYY-MM-DD])
// release-notes-source: v[X.Y.Z] sha256=[hash of the published release body]

// Categories in this order: Features, then Bug fixes, then Improvements. Omit a category
// with no entries. Each entry is a complete sentence in present tense, with a body —
// never a headline-only entry.
// Within a category, group entries by area so same-area entries are adjacent, with
// areas in alphabetical order and source order kept within an area. See release-notes.md.
// Entries are an AsciiDoc definition list: the product area is the term, once
// per category, and the area's entries are a bulleted list under it
// (`Cloud Topics::` then `* Timequeries no longer …`). An area with one entry
// still gets a one-item list. Keep each bullet on one line, and leave a blank
// line between areas. This is a scoped exception to the no-definition-lists
// and no-single-item-lists rules for release-notes pages. See release-notes.md.
=== Features

[Area]::
* [A new capability, in present tense and with no "now" (it has no prior behavior to contrast): "X supports …".]

=== Bug fixes

[Area]::
* [A defect corrected, as a present-tense outcome: "X no longer …" / "X now …". Not "Fixed a bug where …".]
* [Another entry in the same area, in source order.]

[Next area, alphabetically]::
* [An entry in that area.]

=== Improvements

[Area]::
* [Better behavior for an existing capability, in present tense.]

// Footer: link releases before the floor to the public GitHub releases page, which
// keeps hosting historical Redpanda releases.
== Release notes for older versions

Release notes for versions before {earliest-tracked-version} are published on GitHub. See the https://github.com/redpanda-data/redpanda/releases[Redpanda releases page^].
